trajectory_summary: The call opens with an address mismatch and a spontaneous disclosure of the customer's wife's passing, both handled adequately but without emotional depth. The middle third burns roughly 8-9 minutes on a bill-collection tech struggle before the rep correctly pivots to verbal read-back, recovering a customer who was close to disengaging. The close is efficient and protocol-correct: the rep identifies the daughter as co-title-holder and builds the appointment around her schedule, landing a booked time with a specific day and hour.

observed_outcome.quote: Well, I would get you guys down for Monday at seven.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday) and time (7 PM) were locked, and the rep confirmed the daughter (co-title-holder since the wife's passing) would be present, satisfying co-owner inclusion per protocols.spouse_decision logic extended to the daughter.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the bill amount and simply acknowledged it ('Yeah. Okay. Good to know.') before moving straight to the kilowatt-usage ask; the number was never turned into an emotional lever against the utility. The flip should have gone right after the bill amount was given, e.g. reflecting the pain of that $200+ bill before pivoting to the usage-data ask.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: So the only thing I need from you, James, is just a copy of your kilowatt usage on your bill.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: After failed attempts at photo/text and email, the rep pivoted to having the customer read the kWh numbers aloud directly off the paper bill, successfully capturing usage data live on the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked 'what interested you in solar' or an equivalent; the call moved directly from intro into address/roof/title verification without surfacing the customer's underlying motivation.
